note: For x in G, C_G(x) is a subgroup and gC_G(x) maps bijectively to gxg^{-1}; hence the conjugacy class size is [G:C_G(x)]. Lagrange gives |C_G(x)|=p^m. If x is noncentral, C_G(x) is proper, so m<n and its class has size p^{n-m}, divisible by p. The conjugacy classes contained in Z(G) are exactly singletons, yielding |G|=|Z(G)|+sum(noncentral class sizes). Modulo p, p divides |Z(G)|. Since identity lies in Z(G), |Z(G)|>=1; positive divisibility by p>=2 gives |Z(G)|>=2, hence a nonidentity central element.
